brief: August payrolls pushed September Fed-hike odds from roughly 35% to above 60%; hot PPI then sticky CPI pushed odds to about 90%, with futures pricing a 97% chance of at least one more hike by year-end (51bps priced for 2026, versus 60bps of cuts priced in February). Separately, Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb disruptions (Iran hit ships near Hormuz, Houthis seized Mocha and reached Perim island, Saudi crude output fell to 6 mb/d, a three-decade low) pushed oil above 100 dollars and diesel past 6 dollars a gallon, reinforcing the inflation case. Treasury yields sold off across the curve (2Y up 28bps to 4.60%, 30Y to 5.38%, highest since 2007); the ECB hiked 25bp to 2.50% and warned inflation could stay above target through 2027, the BoJ is expected to hike to 1.25%, and the BoE is expected to hold but with a hawkish market shift. Equities fell for the week despite a Friday relief rally as oil pulled back and CPI avoided the worst outcome. Astra briefly lifted AI stocks before those gains reversed, while OpenAI GPT-6 pressured software vendors on margin-erosion fears. Equity funds saw large outflows even as investors rotated into short-duration bonds rather than corporate credit.
